title: Disabled Veterans Real Estate Tax Exemption
summary: Pennsylvania can exempt a Veteran's principal residence from real estate tax if the VA rates the Veteran 100 percent permanently disabled, unemployable, blind, paraplegic, or as having lost two or more limbs, and the State Veterans' Commission finds financial need.
amount: Full exemption from real estate tax on the principal dwelling. There is no partial or scaled exemption.
eligibility: Pennsylvania resident with an Honorable or Under Honorable Conditions discharge from the U.S. Armed Forces
Served during a period of war as determined by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. DMVA says operation-specific or service-specific expeditionary medals can also establish wartime service

Has one of the following from the VA: 100 percent permanent service-connected disability, total disability individual unemployability, service-connected blindness, paraplegia, or loss of two or more limbs
The property is the principal dwelling and is owned solely by the Veteran, jointly with a spouse, or as an estate by the entirety
The State Veterans' Commission must determine that the Veteran has financial need
An unmarried surviving spouse may continue to receive the exemption if the Commission determines need
details: The need test works off a published income level, and there is one right answer rather than two. The statute at 51 Pa.C.S. 8904 set the original rebuttable presumption at $75,000 and requires the State Veterans' Commission to adjust it every two years by the change in the Consumer Price Index. The adjusted figure is published in the Pennsylvania Bulletin.

The current figure is $114,637, effective 1 January 2025. The Commission set it in a notice at 55 Pa.B. 149, published 4 January 2025, applying a 6.1 percent rise in the Northeast all items CPI-U over the two years from 1 November 2022 to 31 October 2024. The previous level was $108,046. Adjustments have been made in 2009, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023 and 2025, so the next one is due 1 January 2027.
That Pennsylvania Bulletin notice is the thing to check, not a county page. One notice every two years covers this figure.

If your household income is above the presumptive level you are not disqualified. You can request a full determination of need under 43 Pa. Code 5.24(d), and you qualify if your allowable monthly expenses exceed your monthly household income. Expenses must be documented, and the calculation includes a cost of living allowance and counts the potential real estate tax itself as an expense.
If you were denied for need before 1 January 2025, DMVA specifically encourages reapplying under the higher level. The effective date runs from the date of the new application.
You apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs in the county where you live, not directly to the state.

Under the statute the county assessment board grants the exemption once the State Veterans' Commission certifies eligibility, and the Commission reviews exemptions periodically. Denials may be appealed to the Adjutant General.
DMVA asks that general questions go to Ra-retx@pa.gov, and that completed applications and personal information not be sent by email.
agency: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs, with the State Veterans' Commission and county assessment offices

title: Educational Gratuity Program for children of disabled or deceased Veterans
summary: Pennsylvania pays a per-semester gratuity directly to an approved Pennsylvania school for the child of a wartime Veteran who is rated 100 percent permanently and totally disabled or who died in service or from a service-connected disability.
amount: Up to $500 per term or semester per qualified child, paid directly to the approved educational institution. Payments run no longer than four scholastic years, which DMVA describes as eight payments.
eligibility: The child is between 16 and 23 years of age. Under 51 Pa.C.S. 8702, if the child turns 23 while completing an educational or training course, payments may continue until that course is completed
The child has lived in Pennsylvania for the five years immediately before applying
The child attends an approved educational institution located in Pennsylvania
The child demonstrates financial need

The Veteran parent had an Honorable or Under Honorable Conditions discharge and served during established wartime service dates as determined by the VA, and is rated 100 percent permanent and total service-connected disabled
Alternatively, the Veteran parent died in service during a period of war or armed conflict
Wartime service can also be established by an Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal, a Navy Expeditionary Medal, or a Marine Corps Expeditionary Medal
details: The expeditionary medal route is worth checking before you rule yourself out. DMVA accepts an Armed Forces, Navy, or Marine Corps Expeditionary Medal as establishing wartime service, which reaches service that does not fall inside a formally declared wartime period.
The money goes to the school, not to the student or the family, and only after the approved institution submits proof that the applicant is matriculated.

DMVA lists the documents to bring: the Veteran's DD214 or military death certificate, the applicant's birth certificate, photo identification such as a driver's licence or voter registration, and proof of five years of Pennsylvania residency.
You apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs in the county where you live.
The statute lets the department adjust the per-term amount to stay within the appropriation, so the payment can be less than the $500 maximum.

DMVA points applicants to the VA WEAMS institution search tool to check whether a Pennsylvania school is approved. General questions go to Ra-eg@pa.gov, and personal information should not be emailed.
agency: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs

title: Veterans' Temporary Assistance for a short-term financial emergency
summary: Pennsylvania offers a limited cash grant to a Veteran or an unmarried surviving spouse who temporarily cannot afford the necessities of life. It covers food, shelter, fuel, and clothing only, and it is meant for a documented immediate emergency.
amount: Up to $1,600 in a 12-month period, per DMVA. The statute itself sets no dollar figure. It caps assistance at the established maximum or the documented amount of need, whichever is less.
eligibility: Honorable discharge from the U.S. Armed Forces documented by a DD Form 214, or died in service or killed in action, or has a service-connected disability certified by the VA
Eligible applicants are the Veteran or the unmarried surviving spouse of a deceased Veteran
Bona fide Pennsylvania resident who does not maintain legal residence in another state
Temporarily unable to afford the necessities of life because of loss of income, assets, or support due to sickness, disability, unemployment, or natural or manmade disaster
Not receiving sufficient assistance from another state or federal agency
Must show a clear and present direct and immediate need
details: The grant is restricted to food, shelter, fuel, and clothing. It is not general-purpose cash.
The statute prohibits paying assistance in the form of relief orders, and lets the department scale amounts to the money available in the fund.
DMVA lists the supporting documents: DD Form 214, proof of residency, documentation of the loss of employment or income, proof of other benefits and income, and receipts for the expenses.
You apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs in the county where you live. A denial can be appealed to the Adjutant General.
General questions go to Ra-vta@pa.gov. DMVA asks that completed applications and personal information not be emailed.
agency: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs

title: Blind Veterans Pension
summary: Pennsylvania pays a state pension to a Veteran whose service-connected injury or disease caused blindness. The statute says it is paid in addition to any other assistance the Veteran receives from the Commonwealth or the federal government.
amount: $150 per month, in addition to other Commonwealth and federal assistance
eligibility: Was a resident of Pennsylvania upon entering military service and listed Pennsylvania as the residence on enlistment
Honorable or Under Honorable Conditions discharge. A dishonorable discharge disqualifies the applicant
A service-connected injury or disease resulted in loss of vision
Visual acuity with correcting lenses of 3/60 or 10/200 or the equivalent, or less, in the better eye, or the visual field of the better eye is contracted to not greater than 20 degrees
details: The Adjutant General determines eligibility and the decision is final under the statute.
You apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs in the county where you live.
DMVA lists the documents that speed processing: a copy of the DD214, proof of Pennsylvania residency at entry into military service, and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs decision letter.
General questions go to RA-MVVeteransPension@pa.gov. Completed applications and personal information should not be emailed.
agency: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs

title: Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans Pension
summary: Pennsylvania pays a state pension to a Veteran who lost, or lost the use of, two or more extremities because of a service-connected injury or disease. It is paid on top of other Commonwealth and federal assistance.
amount: $150 per month, in addition to other Commonwealth and federal assistance
eligibility: Was a Pennsylvania resident upon entering military service and listed the Commonwealth as the residence on enlistment
Honorable or Under Honorable Conditions discharge. A dishonorable discharge disqualifies the applicant
A service-connected injury or disease resulted in the loss, or the permanent and severe or complete paralysis, of two or more limbs
At least a 40 percent disability compensation rating in each of the affected limbs, as certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
details: The Adjutant General determines eligibility and issues the implementing regulations.
You apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs in the county where you live.
DMVA lists the documents that speed processing: a copy of the DD214, proof of Pennsylvania residency at entry into military service, and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs decision letter.
DMVA cites 51 Pa. Consolidated Statutes Chapter 77 and 43 Pa. Code Chapter 5 as the legal authority.
General questions go to RA-MVVeteransPension@pa.gov. Completed applications and personal information should not be emailed.
agency: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs

title: How Pennsylvania taxes military pay and military retired pay
summary: Pennsylvania does not tax federal active duty pay earned outside the state, and does not tax military retired or retainer pay. Military service performed inside Pennsylvania by a Pennsylvania resident is generally taxable compensation.
amount: Retired or retainer pay is exempt from PA personal income tax. Active duty pay earned outside Pennsylvania is not taxable. Active duty pay for service performed inside Pennsylvania is taxable, with a narrow emergency exception.
eligibility: You are a Pennsylvania resident filing a PA personal income tax return
For the out-of-state exclusion, the pay must be for federal active duty or federal active duty for training performed outside Pennsylvania
details: The Department of Revenue states that military pay received while on federal active duty or federal active duty for training outside Pennsylvania is not taxable. Leave it off Line 1a of the PA-40 and attach copies of your W-2 and your military orders with an explanation of the amount excluded. Revenue says it will not process the return without proof the pay was earned outside Pennsylvania.

Income received by a Pennsylvania resident for military service performed inside Pennsylvania is taxable even on federal active duty or active duty for training, unless it is active military duty within Pennsylvania for an emergency under 35 Pa.C.S. Ch. 76.

Reservists and National Guard members ordered to active duty for training under Title 10 or Title 32 are on federal active duty, so the same inside and outside rule applies. Compensation for weekend drills performed inside Pennsylvania remains taxable.

The PA Personal Income Tax Guide states that "Retired or retainer pay of a member or former member of a uniform service calculated under Chapter 71 of Title 10, U.S. Code as amended" is exempt from PA personal income tax.

The same guide excludes from taxable compensation "amounts received as a disability pension, disability annuity, or similar allowance for physical injuries or sickness resulting from active service in the armed forces of the United States."

Watch the Tax Forgiveness trap. Revenue says military pay that you correctly left off the PA-40 should still be included in eligibility income for Tax Forgiveness. Only hazardous duty pay and pay earned in a combat zone are left out of eligibility income.

A Pennsylvania resident serving in a combat zone or qualified hazardous duty area gets the same extension as federally, automatically extended to 180 days from the last day of service or the last day of continuous hospitalization for an injury incurred there. Print COMBAT ZONE at the top of the return and include a copy of your orders.

title: Veterans' preference in Pennsylvania public employment
summary: Pennsylvania adds 10 points to a Veteran's passing civil service examination score and requires appointing authorities to give preference to a qualified Veteran on the eligible list. The same preference extends to certain spouses and surviving spouses.
amount: 10 additional points added to a passing civil service examination score, which then sets the Veteran's standing on the eligible list
eligibility: You served in the armed forces, including a reserve component or the National Guard, completed your initial contractual military service obligation, and your last discharge or release was under conditions other than dishonorable

Or you served during a period of war or armed conflict as determined by the Department of Defense, completed a tour of active duty for purposes other than training, were released from it under conditions other than dishonorable, and continue to serve. This route does not require completing the initial contractual obligation
Or you completed an initial contractual military service obligation and continue to serve

Or you are on active duty completing a tour of three years or more and are within 90 days of an approved discharge or release, evidenced by documentation of the projected discharge under conditions other than dishonorable
Service is documented by discharge papers, separation documents such as a DD214, DD215, or NGB-22, or a statement of service

Under 51 Pa.C.S. 7108 the same preference extends to an unmarried surviving spouse of a deceased service member, and to the spouse of a Veteran the VA has classified as having a permanent total disability
details: Two separate things happen. Section 7103 adds 10 points to a passing civil service appointment examination score, and that new score sets your standing on the eligible list. Section 7104 then requires the appointing authority to give preference to a Veteran whose name appears on that list, notwithstanding the Veteran's standing on it, so long as the appointment is otherwise made under 71 Pa.C.S. 2402.

Section 7105(a) requires appointing authorities to count relevant training or education received during military service in lieu of formal training and education when judging whether you have the requisite qualifications.

Section 7105(b) provides that age, loss of limb, or another physical impairment that does not incapacitate you cannot be used to disqualify you, so long as you can satisfactorily perform in the position.

Section 7107 protects you in a layoff. When a reduction in force is necessary, your years of service are calculated by adding your civil service or public works years to your total years in the armed forces, including a reserve component or National Guard, during any period of war or armed conflict.

Section 7109 makes this chapter the exclusive Veterans' preference law applying to the Commonwealth and to its political subdivisions and municipal agencies, for appointment and for retention. A county or city cannot substitute its own weaker rule.
It is audited. The State Civil Service Commission conducts audits of appointments and changes in employment in the classified service to check strict compliance with the Military Affairs Code.
For the documentation required and where to submit it, see employment.pa.gov, or contact the Governor's Office of Administration at 717-783-6655 or ra-cs-vetpreference@pa.gov.
agency: Pennsylvania State Civil Service Commission and the Governor's Office of Administration
statuteRef: 51 Pa.C.S. Ch. 71 (sections 7101 to 7111), especially sections 7103, 7104, 7105, and 7108

title: Free vehicle registration and Veterans designation on a PA driver license
summary: PennDOT waives registration and title fees on one vehicle for Veterans in several specific categories, including Purple Heart and Medal of Honor recipients and former prisoners of war. Pennsylvania also lets a Veteran add a Veterans designation to a driver license.
amount: Registration and title fees are waived on one passenger vehicle or truck weighing 9,000 pounds or less. License plate fees still apply.
eligibility: Lost a limb, lost an eye, or became partially paralyzed while serving in the U.S. Armed Forces
Was captured by the enemy in an armed conflict for which the Department of Defense authorizes a campaign medal
Was awarded the Congressional Medal of Honor
Was awarded the Purple Heart
details: The waiver covers one passenger vehicle or truck of 9,000 pounds or less. Plate fees are not waived.
The application is PennDOT form MV-371DV, which carries the full eligibility list and the required documentation.
Separately, PennDOT lets a Veteran add a Veterans designation to a standard driver license or to a commercial driver license.

PennDOT also offers military special registration plates, a military status endorsement for active duty members, a military CDL skills test waiver, and a process to register a vehicle in Pennsylvania while assigned out of state or deployed overseas.

PennDOT separately issues Severely Disabled Veteran parking placards. For those, the disability must be service-connected and certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Regional Office Administrator in Philadelphia or Pittsburgh, and PennDOT accepts VA letters showing a 100 percent service-connected disability.

title: Free and reduced-fee hunting and furtaker licenses for disabled Veterans
summary: A Pennsylvania resident Veteran whose wartime disability includes the loss or loss of use of a limb, or who is rated 100 percent disabled by the VA, gets a free hunting or furtaking license. Veterans rated 60 to 99 percent get one at a reduced fee.
amount: No charge for the resident disabled Veteran hunting and furtaker licenses. For a 60 to 99 percent rating the statute sets a $1 license. The Game Commission publishes the reduced disabled Veteran hunting and furtaker license at $2.97.
eligibility: Pennsylvania resident who is a Veteran of a war or armed conflict, with a service-incurred disability

Free license: the disability consists of the loss of one or more limbs, or the loss of the use of one or more limbs, or the Veteran is 100 percent disabled as certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
Reduced-fee license: a disability rating between 60 and 99 percent as certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
The applicant must otherwise qualify and be mentally and physically fit to hunt
The application must state that the applicant is a war or armed conflict Veteran and that the qualifying disability was service incurred
details: You apply to the Game Commission or to a county treasurer. The issuing agent or the Commission may require the applicant's discharge papers.

A Veteran whose qualifying disability is permanent may obtain a lifetime license. The Game Commission lists the resident disabled Veteran lifetime hunting and furtaker licenses, and their renewals, at no charge, and says the lifetime licenses are issued through county treasurers only.
The Game Commission lists a disabled Veteran license replacement at $6.97.
A former prisoner of war may buy a resident hunting license for $1 plus the current issuing fee under the same statute. The Game Commission publishes the prisoner of war hunting license at $2.97.
The Game Commission also publishes resident military, National Guard, and reserves hunting licenses at $2.97.
agency: Pennsylvania Game Commission, and county treasurers

title: Free and reduced-fee fishing licenses for disabled Veterans
summary: A Pennsylvania resident Veteran rated 100 percent service-connected disabled can get a free disabled Veteran lifetime fishing license. A Veteran rated 60 to 99 percent can get a resident fishing license at a reduced fee set by statute at $1.
amount: Free lifetime fishing license at a 100 percent rating, plus a free Combination Trout and Lake Erie Permit. The statute sets the license at $1 for a 60 to 99 percent rating.
eligibility: Pennsylvania resident
Service-connected disability certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
Free lifetime license: rated 100 percent disabled by the VA
Reduced-fee license: rated 60 to 99 percent disabled by the VA
A former prisoner of war certified by the appropriate branch of the armed forces may also obtain a resident fishing license for $1 under the same statute
details: The Fish and Boat Commission states that a Veteran who qualifies for the free license is also issued a Combination Trout and Lake Erie Permit free of charge.
The first license must be obtained in person from a county treasurer, the Fish and Boat Commission's Harrisburg office, or one of the six regional law enforcement offices.

Bring proof of Pennsylvania residency, such as a driver license or other documentation of domicile, and written certification from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs confirming the service-connected disability rating.
After the first verification, annual renewals can be obtained from any issuing agent or online at huntfish.pa.gov.
agency: Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission, and county treasurers

title: Pennsylvania Veterans Homes long-term care admission
summary: Pennsylvania runs six state Veterans Homes offering long-term care. Veterans, their spouses, and surviving spouses may apply. Residents pay a monthly maintenance fee set according to their ability to pay.
eligibility: Served in the U.S. Armed Forces or the Pennsylvania Military Forces and was discharged under honorable conditions
Had Pennsylvania as the home of record upon entry into military service, or is a bona fide Pennsylvania resident. Current Pennsylvania residents receive priority in admissions
Spouses of eligible Veterans and surviving spouses of eligible Veterans may also apply
details: The six homes are the Delaware Valley Veterans' Home in Philadelphia County, the Gino J. Merli Veterans' Center in Lackawanna County, the Hollidaysburg Veterans' Home in Blair County, the Pennsylvania Soldiers' and Sailors' Home in Erie County, the Southeastern Veterans' Center in Chester County, and the Southwestern Veterans' Center in Allegheny County.
A resident makes monthly payments against maintenance fee liability in accordance with the resident's ability to pay.
Admissions are first come, first served, and an admissions committee determines the level of care needed. A decision may be appealed.

DMVA lists conditions that make an applicant ineligible, including a need for mental health care or custody, behavior that threatens the applicant or others, a need for treatment the home cannot provide, unresolved alcoholism or substance abuse, contagious disease, and a felony conviction unless the applicant shows good character and has been conviction-free for at least five years after incarceration.
The homes state that they provide varying levels of care, so confirm which level a specific home offers before applying.
agency: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs
